STEP 1 - Scene: A plain cheese pizza, cut into about six bite-size pieces. One or two are edge/crust pieces from a round pizza, and the rest are rectangular pieces.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A white square dinner plate. I treat it as equivalent to a 26 cm plate, so area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ 530 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: Cheese pizza pieces (crust, tomato sauce, melted mozzarella). No separate sauce or oil is visible beyond the cheese.

STEP 4 - Area: The pizza pieces cover about 40% of the plate, which is about 212 cm². The rest of the plate is empty.

STEP 5 - Volume: 212 cm² × 1.5 cm average height (thick crust plus cheese) ≈ 318 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Pizza is bread-like but has an airy crust, so I use a density of about 0.65 g/ml. 318 ml × 0.65 ≈ 207 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cheese pizza is about 270 kcal/100 g. 207 g × 2.7 ≈ 559 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 200 g is roughly two standard slices' worth of pizza cut into pieces. That is plausible for what is visible.
